questions.question: What are the four top-level categories in CAIS's four-risk framework?
options: Model misalignment, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, and deployment errors
Malicious use, AI races, organizational risks, and rogue AIs
Bioweapons, cyberattacks, disinformation, and autonomous weapons
Capability overhang, reward hacking, goal drift, and deceptive alignment
questions.explanation: CAIS's four-risk framework: (1) malicious use—bad actors using AI to cause harm; (2) AI races—competitive pressure pushing deployment past safe limits; (3) organizational risks—internal lab failures in safety culture, audit, and infosec; (4) rogue AIs—capable AI pursuing goals conflicting with human welfare.

questions.question: What is CAISI and how does it differ from CAIS?
options: CAISI is a European AI safety organization; CAIS is based in the US

CAISI is NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation—a US-government-facing center running voluntary agreements and unclassified capability evaluations; CAIS is a non-profit research org publishing frameworks
CAISI and CAIS are the same organization under different names
CAISI publishes technical safety research; CAIS produces policy recommendations
questions.explanation: CAISI (NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation) operates within the US government, runs voluntary agreements with frontier labs, and publishes unclassified capability evaluations focused on cyber, bio, and chemical-weapons risks. CAIS is an independent 501(c)(3) that publishes frameworks and coordinates public statements. Different missions; the acronyms collide.

questions.question: What did the CAIS May 2023 extinction-risk statement assert?
options: That AI systems currently deployed pose an imminent risk to human life
That mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war
That all frontier AI development should pause until safety is guaranteed
That AI companies should be regulated as utilities to prevent monopolization
questions.explanation: The May 2023 CAIS statement, co-signed by hundreds of professors and company leaders, stated: 'Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.'

questions.question: Which of the four CAIS risk categories is most directly actionable for individual practitioners?
options: Malicious use, because practitioners can add content filters
AI races, because practitioners can advocate for slower deployment
Organizational risks, because safety culture, audit rigor, multi-layered defenses, and information security are directly under a practitioner's control
Rogue AIs, because practitioners can design alignment objectives
questions.explanation: Organizational risk is the most actionable for practitioners. Safety culture (can team members escalate without career cost), rigorous audits (external and internal), multi-layered defenses (no single layer sufficient), and information security (model weights, eval data leaking) are all directly under a practitioner's organizational influence.

questions.question: What would California SB-53 be, if signed, and why does it matter beyond California?
options: A federal AI regulation that applies to all US companies
The first US state-level catastrophic-risk regulation; it matters because state-level regulation has historically led federal action in US tech policy
A voluntary AI safety standard for California companies with no legal enforcement
A funding bill for AI safety research in California universities
questions.explanation: If signed, SB-53 would be the first US state-level catastrophic-risk regulation for frontier AI. It matters beyond California because state-level regulation has historically led federal action in US tech policy. Its framing—capability thresholds, whistleblower protections, incident reporting—shapes what future state and federal legislation will look like.

questions.question: What is the 'final synthesis' the lesson draws from all of Phase 15?
options: A single sufficiently strong safety layer can substitute for the full stack if implemented correctly
Every previous lesson is one layer in a defense-in-depth stack whose completeness matters more than any single layer's strength
External evaluation is the most important safety measure and should receive all investment
Societal governance can substitute for technical controls in low-stakes deployments
questions.explanation: The final synthesis: labs publish scaling policies (Lessons 19-20), external evaluators produce measurements (Lesson 21), civil society tracks and publicizes (CAIS), government runs voluntary programs and baseline regulation (CAISI, SB-53), and practitioners build multi-layered controls (Lessons 10-18). The completeness of the stack matters more than any single layer's strength.
